newsitem.title: GERMANY: German coalition urges approval of EU jobs chapter.
newsitem.headline: German coalition urges approval of EU jobs chapter.

text.p: The parliamentary groups of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's centre-right coalition, signalling a key shift in Germany's policy on monetary union, on Tuesday urged Bonn to approve a proposed jobs chapter in the so-called Maastricht II treaty.
"The federal government should agree to adopt a chapter on employment in the treaty," the coalition parties said in a draft paper obtained by Reuters.
Germany, fearing political interference in the work of a future independent European central bank, had opposed the idea of a jobs chapter for years.

But at a meeting of European economic and finance ministers in Luxembourg this week, the new leftist French government put the brakes on European economic and monetary union (EMU), saying it needed time to think before signing a stability pact aimed at guaranteeing the stability of the single currency.
The draft paper of the German coalition parties also said that tighter coordination of jobs policies on the part of EU members could be possible without transferring additional powers to Brussels.
This could also include a sharper orientation of the European social fund towards jobs-related projects.
